# ADR-NNN — <the choice, stated as a claim>

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD · **Sprint:** NN · **Status:** accepted | superseded by ADR-NNN

**Context.** What forced a decision. Two or three sentences, no history lesson.

**Options.** (a) … (b) … (c) …

**Choice.** Which one, stated flatly.

**Why.** Why this beat the others — including why the rejected options were
plausible. An ADR that makes the alternatives look stupid is not recording a
decision, it is justifying one.

**Cost if wrong.** What it takes to undo this, and what triggers a revisit.

---

*Five lines is the target. Written at the moment the choice is made, never
reconstructed later — a reconstructed ADR records the justification, not the
reasoning.*
